content.content:
Order service API

All responses are JSON unless noted. Requests are made to the address this service is running on.

GET /docs
    This page (plain text).

GET /value
    Returns {"value": <integer>}. No authentication.

POST /token
    Returns {"token": "<token>"}. No authentication. Send the token on authenticated
    requests in the header "Authorization: Bearer <token>".

GET /orders?page=N
    Authenticated. Lists orders, 50 per page; N starts at 1.
    Returns {"page", "total_pages", "items", "next"}. "next" is the path of the following
    page, or null on the last page.
    Each order has: id, customer_id, status, placed_at, amount_cents.
    status is one of: placed, shipped, cancelled, returned.
    placed_at is an ISO 8601 timestamp. amount_cents is an integer number of cents.

GET /customers/{id}
    Authenticated. Returns {"id", "name", "region", "tier", "discount_pct"}; 404 if the id is unknown.
    region is one of: north, south, east, west. discount_pct is a whole-number percentage.

content.text:
I've written `result.json` to the workspace root. Shipped orders placed from 1 March to 31 May 2025 (UTC) come to **9,329,707 cents** after discounts, across **407 distinct orders**.

| Region | Cents |
|---|---|
| north | 2,666,579 |
| south | 2,714,624 |
| east | 1,671,579 |
| west | 2,276,925 |

The four regions add up exactly to the total. I didn't run the calculation a second time to compare.

How it was computed:
- **Pages:** I fetched all 30 pages by following each page's link to the next one, which gave 1,480 distinct orders.
- **Duplicates:** I discarded 20 repeated listings and counted each order id once.
- **Status:** only orders with status exactly "shipped" are counted.
- **Dates:** every timestamp was converted to UTC before checking the range. All of them carried a timezone, so none had to be assumed to be UTC.
- **Discounts:** each order was reduced by its customer's discount and rounded half up to a whole cent, then summed. Each customer was looked up once and reused.
- **Errors:** expired tokens were replaced and failed requests were repeated.

On surprises, the data looked clean. Every customer on a qualifying order was found, and no status values appeared other than the four in the documentation. The only quirk was the 20 duplicates you warned about. I didn't record how often the service rate-limited or expired tokens, so I can't say how much that affected the run.

The working script is in `/tmp/work`, outside the workspace.
